selection_method: Selected only after the 138-record exclusion inventory was committed and read back. Each candidate was compared against published report subjects/mechanism fingerprints. Primary sources are feature/administration/configuration guides; Community pages are scenario sources only.

candidates.lesson_subject: Fortinet Support Tool capture lifecycle: REST API key scope, daemon selection, and 48-hour background capture
candidates.scenario_status: The Community article is old; an activity/comment dated 2026-10-29 notes a logout/login after extension installation, but material-update status could not be confirmed. Treat as an operational note, not a verified new/materially updated 30-day article.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiGate generates expiring REST API capture key → desktop Support Tool connects to selected IP/FQDN/port → scenario/daemons/filters selected → time-bounded capture collected → .fgtcapture/.ftntcap evidence reviewed
candidates.failure_class: GUI or intermittent fault occurs outside a manual debug window; expired key, insufficient admin scope, or missing Chrome extension leaves incomplete capture
candidates.evidence_pattern: key expiry/trusted-host settings; selected daemon list; capture timestamps; resource charts; REST API responses; .fgtcapture/.ftntcap playback; GUI video requires Chrome extension
candidates.remediation_path: verify exact target/protocol/port and key validity; limit trusted hosts; ensure admin has required System read/write; select the failing subsystem and bounded capture window; reproduce fault; correlate video, resource chart, and daemon logs
candidates.question_fingerprint: A capture is created but contains no GUI video; distinguish daemon capture from browser extension capture
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiGate key issuance → desktop Support Tool → daemon/REST capture → optional Chrome GUI capture → evidence timeline

candidates.lesson_subject: SD-WAN overlay templates: generated IPsec/BGP provisioning order versus SD-WAN policy intelligence
candidates.scenario_status: No directly matched Community scenario within the rolling 30-day window was verified; primary feature documentation drives the lesson.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Select hub/branch topology and underlays → wizard generates IPsec/BGP/CLI provisioning templates → assign roles/device groups → install interface templates → IPsec templates → SD-WAN template → verify overlay and SD-WAN rules separately
candidates.failure_class: overlay tunnels or routes absent because template dependencies/install order/underlay reachability are wrong; operator mistakes overlay generation for SD-WAN path selection
candidates.evidence_pattern: generated template list and assignments; installation preview/task; IPsec SA state; BGP neighbors/routes; SD-WAN Monitor health and rule match
candidates.remediation_path: confirm hub-branch underlay reachability; inspect generated templates and target assignments; install in documented dependency order; then install a separate SD-WAN template and validate path rules
candidates.question_fingerprint: BGP/IPsec overlay exists but traffic selection is not intelligent; identify missing SD-WAN template/policy layer
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Topology wizard → generated IPsec/BGP/CLI templates → ordered install → tunnel/BGP evidence → separate SD-WAN rule decision

candidates.lesson_subject: OFTP log encryption negotiation: sender/receiver enc-algorithm compatibility and identity checks
candidates.scenario_status: Older contextual Community troubleshooting example (2024); not presented as a recent 30-day case.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiGate OFTP client initiates connection → server identity/certificate and TLS negotiation → enc-algorithm capabilities compared → OFTP log stream accepted or rejected → device connection status updates
candidates.failure_class: FortiGate cannot establish or sustain secure OFTP logging because encryption level, TLS minimum, server identity, or network path differs
candidates.evidence_pattern: FortiGate config log fortianalyzer setting; FortiAnalyzer enc-algorithm/TLS settings; sniffer at both ends; fgtlogd/miglogd logs; authorized device serial/certificate
candidates.remediation_path: compare sender and receiver algorithm levels and TLS minimums; verify serial/certificate identity; check bidirectional reachability and MTU; align supported settings without downgrading security unnecessarily
candidates.question_fingerprint: A FortiGate reaches FAZ IP but OFTP does not connect; distinguish algorithm/TLS negotiation from routing
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiGate sender → network/TLS → FAZ receiver compatibility gate → OFTP accepted/rejected → log ingest

candidates.lesson_subject: BGP EVPN multihoming: Ethernet Segment ID, designated-forwarder preference, and MAC holdtime
candidates.scenario_status: No directly matched recent Community case was verified; lesson is based on the FortiSwitchOS Administration Guide and release-specific feature documentation.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: CE attaches to two PE/leaf FortiSwitches → shared 10-byte ESI identifies Ethernet Segment → EVPN routes advertise reachability → DF preference selects flood-forwarder → MAC synchronization/holdtime handles route withdrawal
candidates.failure_class: dual-homed endpoint loses or duplicates traffic due to inconsistent ESI, link/trunk identity, DF preference, or stale MAC synchronization
candidates.evidence_pattern: switch trunk ESI fields; BGP EVPN route table; duplicate MAC output; VTEP forwarding and port/trunk state; MAC holdtime configuration
candidates.remediation_path: verify identical Ethernet Segment identity across participating switches, correct trunk/member topology and DF preference, inspect EVPN type-2 routes/duplicate MACs, and tune holdtime only for a demonstrated convergence need
candidates.question_fingerprint: A dual-homed server is reachable on one leaf but flooded traffic misbehaves; identify ESI/DF ownership rather than ordinary STP
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Server CE dual-homed to Leaf A and Leaf B → shared ESI → EVPN control plane → DF-selected flood forwarding

candidates.lesson_subject: RadSec for WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise SSIDs: RADIUS-over-TLS transaction and certificate trust
candidates.scenario_status: No directly matched recent FortiAP RadSec Community case was verified; the lesson is primary-guide-led.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client associates to WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise SSID → EAP exchange via AP/controller → FortiGate RADIUS client opens TCP/TLS to server → server certificate/trust validates → RADIUS Access-Accept/Reject → VLAN/policy applied
candidates.failure_class: 802.1X authentication fails despite RF association because RadSec transport, certificate trust/name, NAS identity, or server-side client policy is wrong
candidates.evidence_pattern: RADIUS object transport-protocol tcp and server address; TLS handshake/certificate chain; RADIUS server client logs; EAP/RADIUS result; assigned VLAN and DHCP lease
candidates.remediation_path: verify compatible FortiOS/FortiAP release and SSID mode; configure TCP/TLS RADIUS transport and certificate trust; align NAS-IP/NAS-ID and server client definition; test EAP and authorization separately
candidates.question_fingerprint: Client associates but never receives Access-Accept over RadSec; identify TLS/RADIUS boundary rather than RF issue
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Wi-Fi client → AP/controller EAP → FortiGate RadSec TLS client → RADIUS server certificate/auth policy → Access-Accept/Reject

candidates.lesson_subject: IPv6 endstation access versus IPv4-only network-device discovery and inventory
candidates.scenario_status: No directly matched recent IPv6-specific Community case was verified.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: IPv6 host/device reaches eth0/eth1 portal or agent → host/adapter record displays IPv6 → network-device inventory discovery/polling still requires IPv4 management address → L3 IP-to-MAC visibility depends on supported switch/vendor
candidates.failure_class: IPv6 endpoint can reach portal but is not fully visible/enforced as expected; operator assumes IPv6 support means IPv6 network-device discovery
candidates.evidence_pattern: Host View/Adapter View address fields; portal/agent reachability over IPv6; eth0 admin access; inventory device IP and polling support list
candidates.remediation_path: separate endpoint communication from infrastructure discovery; retain an IPv4 management address for supported inventory devices; verify L3 polling vendor support and validate host identity across IPv4/IPv6 addresses
candidates.question_fingerprint: IPv6 host reaches the portal but switch inventory discovery fails; identify the documented capability boundary
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: IPv6 endpoint → FortiNAC portal/agent succeeds; separate network-device inventory lane remains IPv4 management-dependent

candidates.lesson_subject: Directory synchronization for machine-auth RBAC: separate host/user groups and AD primaryGroupID caveat
candidates.scenario_status: Community case dated 2026-09-16, outside the 30-day window; retained as older contextual failure evidence, not labeled recent.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: LDAP/AD directory sync → FortiNAC-F creates <group>_host and <group>_user projections → EAP-TLS machine authentication registers host → User/Host Profile checks synchronized group → Network Access Policy match or default network
candidates.failure_class: Machine authentication succeeds but expected access policy does not match because AD membership exists only through primaryGroupID and not the group's member attribute
candidates.evidence_pattern: FortiNAC-F synchronized host-group member count; Policy Details Groups not matched; AD member/memberOf and primaryGroupID; scheduler synchronization result
candidates.remediation_path: verify sync selection and task completion; inspect actual AD member attribute versus primaryGroupID; use supported normal group membership or supported primary-group approach; resynchronize and re-check Policy Details
candidates.question_fingerprint: EAP-TLS succeeded but host remains on registration network and synced _host group has zero members
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: AD group membership source → scheduled sync → _host/_user group projections → machine auth → User/Host Profile → policy/default VLAN

candidates.lesson_subject: SAML IdP signing-certificate auto-rotation before expiry
candidates.scenario_status: No directly matched recent Community case for scheduled SAML IdP certificate rotation was verified.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Admin imports new IdP signing certificate → selects current/default and replacement certificate → sets switch date/time before old expiry → IdP begins signing assertions with new cert → SP trusts new certificate/metadata
candidates.failure_class: SAML login breaks at certificate rollover because IdP signing key changes before the service provider trusts the replacement or the switch time is wrong
candidates.evidence_pattern: SAML IdP General default certificate and new default certificate; configured switch timestamp; assertion signature/certificate; SP trust/metadata and SAML response logs
candidates.remediation_path: import and distribute replacement certificate ahead of time; coordinate SP trust/metadata update; configure and verify switch time; test a pilot SP and monitor signature validation around cutover
candidates.question_fingerprint: IdP auto-switches at the planned time but SP rejects assertions; distinguish signing-certificate trust from user authentication
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Current IdP cert + staged replacement → scheduled cutover → signed SAML assertion → SP trust validation → success/failure

candidates.lesson_subject: Secret checkout lock lifecycle: active launcher session delays forced checkout
candidates.scenario_status: Community article is dated 2026-08-26. Search results showed recent forum activity, but a precise material-update date was not confirmed; do not classify it as a verified new/materially updated 30-day scenario.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: User checks out secret → secret becomes exclusively assigned for checkout duration → launcher creates active proxy session → admin force-checkout remains blocked while launch is alive → launch ends → idle timer elapses → force checkout can proceed
candidates.failure_class: Secret appears overdue but administrator cannot reclaim it because the privileged session is still active or force-checkout idle timer has not elapsed
candidates.evidence_pattern: secret checkout state/duration; active launch status; last-launch-time; checkout-duration; force-checkout-idle-time; session termination and elapsed idle time
candidates.remediation_path: confirm Requires Checkout and permissions; inspect active launcher and checkout timers; terminate the session safely, wait for idle threshold, then reclaim; do not shorten locks blindly without reviewing privileged-session risk
candidates.question_fingerprint: Checkout duration expired but force-checkout remains unavailable; identify active-launch and idle-timer gates
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Secret checkout → active launcher session holds lock → session termination → idle timer → admin force checkout → next approved user

candidates.lesson_subject: CMDB business-service records: service inventory context and maintenance state versus raw event evidence
candidates.scenario_status: No directly matched recent Community scenario for business-service CMDB mapping was verified.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: CMDB service record maps service name/type to running-on CI and access IP → operator reviews details and maintenance state → event/incident is correlated with service inventory context → analyst verifies underlying device/event evidence separately
candidates.failure_class: Incident triage misattributes impact because business-service ownership/maintenance context is missing or stale; service record is mistaken for live availability proof
candidates.evidence_pattern: CMDB Business Services service list; Type/Name/Running on/Access IP/Details/Maintenance fields; linked CI health and raw event timestamps
candidates.remediation_path: verify the service-to-CI mapping and maintenance metadata; confirm the underlying CI and raw events are current; update stale service records and avoid treating CMDB presence as synthetic availability
candidates.question_fingerprint: A business service record exists but the application is failing; distinguish CMDB relationship metadata from live health evidence
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Business-service CMDB record → running-on CI/access IP → maintenance context → raw event/health evidence → analyst impact assessment

candidates.lesson_subject: Steering bypass destinations: dynamic FQDN routes and on-net/off-net conditional split tunneling
candidates.scenario_status: Older contextual Community case dated 2025-07-21; useful for the symptom that local printer traffic remains tunneled until bypass rules are received after reconnect.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Endpoint receives profile → destination type matched (infrastructure/FQDN/local app/subnet) → FQDN resolves to dynamic route or app/subnet bypass applies → on-net/off-net condition evaluated → traffic uses physical interface instead of cloud tunnel
candidates.failure_class: Trusted local or high-bandwidth traffic still traverses FortiSASE because destination is absent from profile, condition does not match, FQDN/wildcard is unsupported, or endpoint has not reconnected to receive new routes
candidates.evidence_pattern: endpoint profile and bypass destination type; on-net detection result; endpoint route table; traceroute; FortiSASE tunnel/session logs; behavior before/after reconnect
candidates.remediation_path: verify assigned endpoint profile and exact destination object; avoid wildcard FQDN; check on-net/off-net condition and platform support; reconnect endpoint and confirm route/traffic exits locally
candidates.question_fingerprint: Local printer is still tunneled after bypass configuration; identify profile delivery and endpoint route evidence
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiSASE endpoint profile → destination matcher and on-net state → dynamic route/bypass → local physical interface or cloud tunnel

candidates.lesson_subject: ADVPN 2.0 edge discovery and path management: shortcut selection from both spokes' underlay health
candidates.scenario_status: Older Community case dated 2025-04-29; used only as contextual diagnostic example, not a recent 30-day scenario.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Spokes learn peer edge/underlay information → local and remote underlay/link-health criteria evaluated → shortcut query sent to remote spoke → compatible direct shortcut negotiated → SD-WAN service chooses healthy shortcut or falls back to hub
candidates.failure_class: Traffic remains hub-routed because no viable common underlay/path satisfies both spokes' link health and transport criteria
candidates.evidence_pattern: ADVPN 2.0 enablement/version; IKE debug for shortcut-query/rejection; VPN Events ADVPN Shortcut flag; BGP/routes and SD-WAN service state; underlay SLA state on both spokes
candidates.remediation_path: confirm all peers use compatible ADVPN 2.0 configuration and IPv4 support; inspect both spokes' underlay/member health and transport groups; verify shortcut-query/negotiation logs; retain hub path while correcting path eligibility
candidates.question_fingerprint: Spokes have reachability through hub but no shortcut and log says no viable shortcut; identify common underlay/path eligibility
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Hub-and-spoke underlays → edge discovery → both-spoke path-health/transport match → direct shortcut or hub fallback
